title: Consideration and forms of action
summary: The chapter traces how older forms helped shape the bargain requirement.
notes: Covenant, debt, and assumpsit began with different predicates and remedies. The seal supplied a formal basis in covenant; debt focused on a quid pro quo; assumpsit’s development permitted enforcement of promises in ways that affected the need for consideration. The notes explain the later acceptance of reciprocal promises. These historical origins help explain doctrinal language without mechanically deciding modern disputes.
